conceptual-separation.local: Two arbitrary things with nothing in common.
conceptual-separation.limit: Axiom V is interpreted as absence of conceptual dependence. This is an intermediate lemma, not a numbered proposition.

E1-P3.local: Two arbitrary things with nothing in common.
E1-P3.limit: Knowledge of a cause is represented by conceptual dependence. The logical implication is checked; this reading of knowledge still requires philosophical review.

E1-P6-C.local: A substance and a distinct proposed cause.
E1-P6-C.limit: The proof excludes the encoded causal relation. Production is not a separately formalized relation.

adequate-not-partial.local: The same cause and the same effect.
adequate-not-partial.limit: A definitional consequence of the chosen adequate/partial cause encoding, not a numbered proposition.

active-not-passive.local: The same actor and the same event.
active-not-passive.limit: Excludes simultaneous activity and passivity only for this actor-event pair, not every combination of action and passion in a person.

E1-P1.local: A substance and its distinct mode.
E1-P1.limit: Priority by nature is interpreted as asymmetric conceptual dependence. Other meanings of priority have not been proved equivalent.

E1-P6.limit: Uses the alternative corollary argument. The original proof through P2/P3/P5 and the broader notion of production remain unformalized.

E1-P5.local: Two actually existing substances of the same nature.
E1-P5.limit: The general multiplicity principle is assumed, not proved. The theorem says nothing about sharing a single attribute. It uses the later scholium instead of the original demonstration.
E1-P5.textualNote: The Latin proof cites Definition III and Axiom VI here; the imported Elwes proof prints Definitions III and VI. The library preserves that edition. This reference difference must be resolved against the Latin before reconstructing the original proof.

E1-P7.local: A substance already assumed to exist actually.
E1-P7.limit: Essential existence remains a primitive predicate in this version. The intrinsic/external explanation alternative is assumed. No existing substance or God is thereby established.

E1-P8.local: A substance already assumed to exist actually.
E1-P8.limit: Only distinct actual same-nature limiters are excluded. Modal necessity is absent. The limiter classification is used by this proof route but is not a minimal logical requirement of the stronger multiplicity premise.

attribute-inclusion.local: A substance and another substance whose essential aspects it includes.
attribute-inclusion.limit: An intermediate lemma in the attribute vocabulary. Reality inclusion is defined on essential aspects. The selected representation principle connects perception to those aspects; completeness is not needed for this step.

E1-P9.local: Two substances with strictly nested sets of essential aspects. Their existence is not established by this proof.
E1-P9.limit: Restricted to substances and a structural reading of more reality. Strict set inclusion does not imply greater infinite cardinality. Representation and coverage are explicit interpretive premises, not the historical proof established from Definition IV alone. This attribute vocabulary has not been identified with the older causal or modal vocabulary.

E1-P10.local: An attribute perceived as constituting the essence of a substance.
E1-P10.limit: Conceived through itself means absence of external conceptual requirements in this vocabulary. Transferring a requirement from attribute to substance is an additional interpretation; a compiled countermodel shows that D3 and primitive D4 alone do not justify that transfer. The scholium is not formalized.

E1-P2.local: Two substances with no shared attribute.
E1-P2.limit: The conclusion follows from the selected semantic bridge. This does not reconstruct the historical claim that Definition III alone suffices, nor infer absence of commonality from absence of dependence. Different profiles with an overlap do not meet the local hypothesis.

E1-P4.local: Two distinct entities of the qualitative vocabulary.
E1-P4.limit: Qualities are represented by attributes or modifications, and matching all qualities implies identity. These are disclosed additions to the primitive vocabulary. The proof obtains a distinguishing attribute or modification, using classical reasoning; it is not just a classification into two kinds of entity.
E1-P4.textualNote: The Latin proof cites Definition IV for attributes. The Elwes English transcription in the library says Axiom IV at that point; the Latin reference is used here.

E1-P5-attributes.local: Two substances sharing at least one attribute.
E1-P5-attributes.limit: This route addresses sharing one attribute, unlike the older same-nature reconstruction. Its complete-essence and injective-abstraction premises are substantial: compiled countermodels show that removing either can permit distinct substances sharing an attribute. P1 alone has not justified abstraction. This remains a conditional reconstruction.
E1-P5-attributes.textualNote: The Latin proof uses Definition III and Axiom VI when setting modifications aside. The Elwes transcription labels the latter Definition VI; our abstraction interpretation is disclosed separately.

E1-P6-attributes.local: Two distinct substances in the shared causal and qualitative vocabulary.
E1-P6-attributes.limit: The compiled argument now follows the dependency route V → II → III → VI. It inherits the disclosed interpretation of each step. The predicate causes represents production in this restricted reconstruction; no full modal theory of production is established.

universal-substance-unique.local: A given substance g having every attribute instantiated by any substance. This existence premise is local to the implication.
universal-substance-unique.limit: A preparatory implication, not a proof of XIV. It does not supply P11, God’s existence, absolute infinity, or the exclusion of conceiving another substance. A compiled model satisfies all selected bridges with two substances and no universal substance. XIV therefore remains outside the numbered Lean coverage.

substance-mode-classification.local: An arbitrary entity in the chosen vocabulary.
substance-mode-classification.limit: The classification follows by cases on Axiom I after adding the two semantic bridges. Being in itself alone does not formally supply conceptual independence; being in another alone does not identify that other as a substance. These missing links are selectable premises.

everything-in-universal-substance.local: A given universal substance g, under exactly the same local premise as the conditional uniqueness step.
everything-in-universal-substance.limit: A preparatory classification toward XV. It proves inherence and conceptual dependence of each mode on the assumed universal substance. It does not prove existence of God or the modal impossibility of existence without God. XV remains source-only in the numbered coverage.
